text:
Sam.AE: Ping — VerdantHealth wants to POC verdant-30b in their colo (internal: verdant-poc). Requirements: KV prefix caching, BYO HSM via PKCS#11, and ~10 qps sustained. They specifically asked about Private SLA (99.9) and proof of no model egress. Need compatibility checklist, rough lead time, and a cost ballpark. Any immediate red flags?

Irene.SE: Quick: verdant-30b upstream uses RMSNorm + grouped_gemm + a nonstandard rotary scale. We can support q8_0 or q4_0 but grouped_gemm perf path requires the kernel patch in runtime >= 2.6.0. Without the patch quantized latency will be worse.

Jon.ML: Conversion notes: export + quantize + compile + smoke perf = ~2 business days if runtime has patch. If not, add 1 day to recompile runtime with grouped_gemm kernel. KV prefix caching works out to ~2048 tokens by default; longer prefixes need kv-shard or prefix-slicing. Distilled option verdant-lite (~13B) available if they want lower cost.

Devin.Infra: On-prem preflight: need NVIDIA driver >=525, CUDA >=12.1, container runtime >=1.6, and PKCS#11 vendor libs present. If they're air-gapped, we can provide an image tarball (adds ~1 day). Ask them to paste outputs of `nvidia-smi` and `ldconfig -p`.

Priya.Security: We support BYO HSM via PKCS#11 in Private with our KMS shim, including key-wrapping and HSM-backed seals. Required artifacts: completed security questionnaire, network/dataflow diagram, SOC2 Type II, signed DPA, and a pen-test summary. For guaranteed zero-evidence model residency we need to validate container image pull method and confirm no egress telemetry; that's negotiable in the contract but requires an ops checklist.

ops-bot: INF ticket created: INF-11722 (verdant private preflight). Suggested commands for customer to run:
```
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,name --format=csv
./validate_cuda.sh --min-version=12.1
ldconfig -p | grep -i pkcs11 || echo "pkcs11 missing"
cat /etc/os-release
```

Irene.SE: Cost note: rough hosted-equivalent for 4x H100s ~ $430/hr platform (ballpark). Private adds platform license + managed ops retainer; to get 99.9% SLA + 24/7 on-call expect an ops retainer. I'll draft 10 qps numbers for Dedicated vs Private.

Jon.ML: Timeline: assuming infra checks pass and they allow runtime patching: 2 days conversion + 1 day KV perf tuning + 1 day integration/docs + 1 day canary = ~5 business days. If we must deliver air-gapped images or recompile runtime on their hardware it pushes to ~7 business days.

Sam.AE: They asked about functional testing with PHI-free sample data and an attestation that model weights do not leave the cluster. Priya, can we provide an attestation template?

Priya.Security: We can provide a model-residency attestation (legal+ops signature) and an ops checklist for preventing egress (no outbound routes, no telemetry collectors). That will be included in the Private SOW addendum. I'll send the RFI template and attestation sample.

Devin.Infra: Note: PKCS#11 vendors differ; ask them to confirm vendor and version. Some older pkcs11 impls need glue wrappers. Also confirm their kernel/new container runtime supports `--device=/dev/nvhost` (container GPU access).

Irene.SE: Variant note: if they accept lower throughput or lower fidelity, verdant-lite (~13B) will run on 2x A100s and cuts infra cost ~40-60% depending on latency target. Also offers simpler onboarding (no grouped_gemm kernel dependency).

Sam.AE: Action items: I'll request `nvidia-smi` + `ldconfig -p` and the filled security RFI. Irene please prepare the 10 qps cost calc + SOW stub for Private vs Dedicated (include attestation clause). Jon pencil in conversion slots (2 days). Priya please send RFI + attestation template. Devin keep INF-11722 open for infra validation.

Irene.SE: Will do — will include both q8_0 and q4_0 cost/latency estimates and the verdant-lite option.

Jon.ML: FYI for perf: without grouped_gemm kernel we may see 15-30% latency regression on tail. Call it out in SOW so expectations are clear.

Sam.AE: Thanks team — I'll update once customer returns env dump and RFI. :thumbsup:
